hindi: “तुम और मैं भूमि पाते हैं” — यह भूमि-सन्धि है।
english: “You and I obtain land” — such is the treaty of land.
notes: labhāvahe is 1st dual present middle, "we two obtain"; a hortative sense ("let us two obtain") is possible. The quotation is closed by iti, which also opens the label bhūmi-sandhi (glossary: closing particle, label rendered "Such is X").

words.gloss: one whose matter is at hand

hindi: उन दोनों में से जिसका प्रयोजन सामने उपस्थित है, जो सम्पन्न भूमि प्राप्त करता है, वह छल लेता है।
english: Of the two, he whose purpose is at hand, who obtains excellent land, outwits [the other].
notes: pratyupasthita-artha taken literally as "having the matter/purpose come to hand"; the exact sense (ready, present) is open. Object of atisandhatte is not stated. Token "so 'tisandhatte" splits into saḥ + atisandhatte (avagraha for a-).

hindi: सम्पन्न की अप्राप्ति समान होने पर, जो बलवान् पर आक्रमण करके भूमि प्राप्त करता है, वह छल लेता है।
english: When the non-obtaining of excellent [land] is equal, he who, having attacked a strong [king], obtains land outwits [the other].
notes: sampanna.alābhe is read literally as sampanna + alābha (non-obtaining of the excellent); the alternative reading sampanna-lābhe ("when the gain of excellent land is equal") is possible if alābhe is a sandhi/typing variant. The noun with tulye and the object of atisandhatte are not stated.

hindi: क्योंकि भूमि-लाभ, शत्रु का क्षीण करना और प्रताप प्राप्त करता है।
english: For [he] obtains the acquisition of land, the weakening of the enemy, and prowess.
notes: Subject not stated (continues from the one who outwits). pratāpa taken as prowess (literally "heat").

hindi: दुर्बल से भूमि-लाभ होने पर सचमुच सरलता होती है।
english: When land is acquired from a weak [king], there is truly ease.

text_flags.why: possible stray dot: the ablative durbalāt is a separate word (as in unit 9 cala.amitrād.bhūmi.lābhe, same pattern in units 23, 26)

notes: The dot after durbalād joins an ablative to a compound; read as two words. satyam taken as "truly" (adverb); alternative "indeed".

hindi: और भूमि-लाभ दुर्बल ही है, और उसका सामन्त, मित्र, शत्रु-भाव को जाता है।
english: And the acquisition of land is weak indeed, and his neighbouring chief, an ally, goes to the state of an enemy.
notes: The first clause is elliptical and rendered literally; the likely sense is that the land acquired from a weak king is itself weak (or that the gain is only of the weak), but the text does not say. tat-sāmanta: tat refers to the one acquiring or the one from whom land is taken, not stated. mitram taken as in apposition to the neighbouring chief.

hindi: बलवत्ता समान होने पर जो स्थित शत्रु को उखाड़कर भूमि प्राप्त करता है, वह छल लेता है।
english: When superior strength is equal, he who, having uprooted an established enemy, obtains land outwits [the other].
notes: sthita-śatru ("standing/established enemy") is rendered literally; the contrast intended is not stated here. The object of atisandhatte is not stated.

words.gloss: barring of enemies and forest tribes

hindi: क्योंकि दुर्ग की प्राप्ति अपनी भूमि की रक्षा और शत्रु और वन-जातियों का प्रतिषेध करती है।
english: For the obtaining of a fort makes the protection of one's own ground and the barring of enemies and forest tribes.
notes: amitra.aṭavī is taken as a dvandva (enemies and forest tribes, aṭavī as in glossary 8.1) governed by pratiṣedha; "karoti" is rendered "makes" (effects).

hindi: चल शत्रु से भूमि-लाभ में शक्य सामन्त वाले की अपेक्षा विशेषता है।
english: In the acquisition of land from a fickle enemy, there is a distinction as against [that with] possible neighbouring chiefs.

text_flags.why: possible stray dot after the ablative cala.amitrād (same pattern as units 5, 23, 26)

notes: Very elliptical. cala = unsteady/fickle; śakya = possible/practicable (not elaborated); śakya-sāmantataḥ with the -tas suffix is read as ablative of comparison ("than/as against"). Which of the two is superior is not stated in the unit; unit 10 gives the reason for the weak/manageable neighbours.

words.gloss: [land] of quick strengthening, acquisition and security

hindi: क्योंकि दुर्बल सामन्तों वाली शीघ्र पुष्टि, योग और क्षेम वाली होती है।
english: For [land] having weak neighbouring chiefs becomes one of quick strengthening, acquisition and security.
notes: The feminine forms imply bhūmiḥ (land), not stated. yoga-kṣema = acquisition and security (glossary); āpyāyana = swelling, strengthening, replenishing.

hindi: विपरीत भूमि बलवान् सामन्तों वाली और कोश और सेना को काट देने वाली होती है।
english: The land that is the opposite, having strong neighbouring chiefs and cutting off treasury and army, comes to be.

text_flags.why: possible missing compound dot: balavat is the first member of the bahuvrīhi balavat-sāmantā (cf. unit 10 durbala.sāmantā)

notes: daṇḍa = army (glossary prakṛti list). The unit reads as the opposite of unit 10.

hindi: “सम्पन्न, नित्य शत्रु वाली अथवा मन्द गुण वाली, अनित्य शत्रु वाली भूमि” — “सम्पन्न, नित्य शत्रु वाली भूमि श्रेष्ठ है, क्योंकि सम्पन्न भूमि कोश और सेना को सिद्ध करती है, और वे दोनों शत्रु का प्रतिघात करने वाले हैं,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: “Excellent land with permanent enemies, or land of weak qualities with temporary enemies” — “Excellent land with permanent enemies is better, for excellent [land] provides treasury and army, and those two are repellers of the enemy,” say the teachers.
notes: The first iti closes the alternatives (no opening quotation mark is printed); the second quotation is the teachers' view, closed by ity ācāryāḥ (glossary: "..., say the teachers"). The quotation is continued by the next unit (na iti kauṭilyaḥ), so it is not flagged. śreyasī = better (comparative of śreyas). sampādayati (caus.) = brings about/provides. amitra-pratighātaka: pratighāta = repulse, warding off.

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.
notes: Formula "na iti X" as in glossary (12.1).

words.gloss: in the non-obtaining of a permanent enemy

hindi: नित्य शत्रु की अप्राप्ति में शत्रु-लाभ अधिक होता है।
english: In the non-obtaining of a permanent enemy, the acquisition of enemies is greater.
notes: Read literally with alābha (non-obtaining). The sense looks contradictory, so another reading is possible: nitya-amitra-lābhe, "in obtaining [land with] permanent enemies, the acquisition of enemies is greater" (a typed-text or sandhi question: nityāmitra-alābhe vs. -ālābhe). Not changed in the text. Compare unit 3 sampanna.alābhe.

hindi: और नित्य शत्रु उपकार किए जाने पर और अपकार किए जाने पर शत्रु ही होता है, किन्तु अनित्य शत्रु उपकार से अथवा अपकार न करने से शान्त होता है।
english: And a permanent enemy, when benefited and when harmed, is an enemy indeed; but a temporary enemy is pacified by a favour or by non-injury.
notes: upakṛte and apakṛte are locative absolutes (the person is not named).

hindi: क्योंकि जिस भूमि के बहुत दुर्गों वाले सीमान्त चोरों के दलों से अथवा म्लेच्छों और वन-जातियों से सदा रहित नहीं हैं, वह नित्य शत्रु वाली है, किन्तु विपरीत स्थिति में अनित्य शत्रु वाली।
english: For that land whose frontier [regions], with many forts, are never free from bands of thieves or from mlecchas and forest tribes, is one with permanent enemies; but in the opposite case, one with temporary enemies.

text_flags.why: possible missing visarga: the genitive feminine relative is yasyāḥ; the double genitive yasyāḥ ... bhūmeḥ is also odd, so the reading is doubtful

notes: yasyā ... bhūmeḥ gives two genitives for one idea; taken as "whose, of the land". pratyantāḥ rendered "frontier [regions]" (could be frontier peoples). aṭavī = forest tribes as in glossary 8.1; mleccha kept as a name.

hindi: “छोटी निकट वाली अथवा बड़ी व्यवहित भूमि” — “छोटी निकट वाली श्रेष्ठ है।”
english: “Land that is small and near, or large and separated” — “The small, near [land] is better.”
notes: The first iti closes the alternatives (a question put by an unnamed view); the second part is the answer. No opening quotation mark is printed. vyavahita = separated/intervened (by other territory), taken literally.

hindi: क्योंकि प्राप्त करने, रक्षा करने और सहायता पहुँचाने में सुगम होती है।
english: For [it] is easy to obtain, to protect and to reinforce.
notes: The feminine sukhā refers to the small, near land of unit 17 (bhūmiḥ). abhisārayitum is the causative of abhi-√sṛ; "reinforce" follows the glossary abhisāra = reinforcement.

hindi: विपरीत व्यवहित है।
english: The opposite is the separated [land].
notes: Elliptical: the separated land is the opposite of what unit 18 says (hard to obtain, protect and reinforce). Not stated in the Sanskrit.

hindi: “दोनों व्यवहित भूमियों में भी सेना द्वारा धारण की जाने वाली अथवा स्वयं धारण की जाने वाली भूमि” — “स्वयं धारण की जाने वाली श्रेष्ठ है।”
english: “Even of two separated [lands], land held by the army or land held by itself” — “The one held by itself is better.”
notes: daṇḍa-dhāraṇā / ātma-dhāraṇā are abstract nouns ("holding by army / by itself"); the reading "held by an army" vs "needing an army to hold it" is open (unit 21 explains: held by its own treasury and army). daṇḍa = army here. The hyphen joins two real words (two entries). No opening quotation mark is printed.

hindi: क्योंकि वह अपने से उत्पन्न कोश और सेना द्वारा धारण की जाती है।
english: For it is held by the treasury and army arisen from itself.
notes: sā refers to the land held by itself (ātma-dhāraṇā).

hindi: विपरीत सेना द्वारा धारण करना है, सेना का स्थान।
english: The opposite is holding by the army, a station of the army.
notes: Elliptical; daṇḍa-sthāna read literally as "station/place of the army" (daṇḍa = army). The unit may also be read "the opposite is holding by the army, [which is] a standing-place of the army".

hindi: “मूर्ख से अथवा बुद्धिमान् से भूमि-लाभ” — “मूर्ख से भूमि-लाभ श्रेष्ठ है।”
english: “Acquisition of land from a fool or from a wise [man]” — “Acquisition of land from a fool is better.”

text_flags.why: possible stray dot after the ablative bāliśād (same pattern as units 5, 9, 26); also in the same line bhūmi.lābha iti is sandhi for bhūmi.lābhaḥ iti

notes: bāliśa = childish, foolish. The quotation has no opening mark; the second quotation is the answer.

hindi: क्योंकि सरलता से प्राप्त होने वाली, पालन किए जाने योग्य होती है और वापस न लिए जाने योग्य।
english: For [it] is easily obtained, [easily] maintained, and not retakable.
notes: The su- of suprāpyā is carried over to anupālyā in brackets only for sense (the Sanskrit does not repeat it). apratyādeya = not retakable (glossary 9.4: ādeya/pratyādeya).

hindi: विपरीत बुद्धिमान् से अनुरक्त है।
english: The opposite [land], from a wise [man], is attached.
notes: Elliptical. anurakta = attached/devoted; to whom (the former ruler, or the people to the land) is not stated. Another reading: "the opposite, from a wise [man], [is] attached" as a separate remark on the wise man's land.

words.gloss: of the one to be afflicted and the one to be uprooted
from the one to be uprooted

hindi: पीड़न किए जाने योग्य और उच्छेद किए जाने योग्य में से उच्छेद किए जाने योग्य से भूमि-लाभ श्रेष्ठ है।
english: Of the one to be afflicted and the one to be uprooted, the acquisition of land from the one to be uprooted is better.
notes: The two gerundives (pīḍanīya, ucchedanīya) name persons (enemies); the genitive dual is read as partitive. pīḍana = affliction (glossary 8.4).

hindi: क्योंकि उच्छेद किए जाने योग्य, आश्रयहीन अथवा दुर्बल आश्रय वाला, आक्रमण किए जाने पर कोश और सेना को लेकर हट जाने की इच्छा रखने वाला, प्रकृतियों द्वारा त्याग दिया जाता है; दुर्ग और मित्र के सहारे टिका हुआ पीड़न किए जाने योग्य नहीं।
english: For the one to be uprooted—without support or with a weak support—when attacked, desirous of retreating with treasury and army taken, is abandoned by his constituent elements; not [so] the one to be afflicted, propped by fort and ally.
notes: The verb of the last clause is not stated ("is abandoned" understood). pratiṣṭabdha is taken as "propped, firmly supported" (literally also "obstructed/stiffened"). apasartu-kāma is apasartum + kāma (the m of the infinitive dropped in the compound). prakṛti = constituent element (glossary).

words.gloss: of the two propped by a fort
of the one with a land fort and the one with a river fort
from the one with a land fort

hindi: दुर्ग के सहारे टिके दोनों में भी स्थल-दुर्ग वाले और नदी-दुर्ग वाले में से स्थल-दुर्ग वाले से भूमि-लाभ श्रेष्ठ है।
english: Even of two propped by a fort—[the one] with a land fort and [the one] with a river fort—the acquisition of land from [the one] with a land fort is better.
notes: durgīya = "belonging to a fort" (of the stated kind); the ablative dual is read as partitive, as in unit 26. sthala = dry land (as against river).

words.gloss: with blockade, crushing and assault easy

hindi: क्योंकि स्थलीय सुगम अवरोध, मर्दन और आक्रमण वाला है, और अनिःश्रावि शत्रु वाला।
english: For the [fort] of the dry land is one with easy blockade, crushing and assault, and with an aniḥśrāvi enemy.

text_flags.why: h written for visarga: aniḥ- (the Devanagari also has ह्)

notes: "Fort" (durga) is not stated; sthāleya is neuter, agreeing with durga understood. Whether su- governs avamarda and avaskanda as well as rodha is uncertain. aniḥśrāvi is obscure (literally perhaps "not flowing out"; cf. niḥ-√sru or niḥ-√śru) and is left untranslated in the English and Hindi; no sense is guessed. avamarda = crushing, avaskanda = assault (glossary).

hindi: किन्तु नदी-दुर्ग दुगुना क्लेश करने वाला है, और जल रक्षणीय है और शत्रु की जीविका करने वाला।
english: But a river fort causes twofold hardship, and the water is to be guarded and provides livelihood to the enemy.
notes: pātavya is from √pā: "to be guarded" (√pā protect) or "to be drunk" (√pā drink); "guarded" is chosen, the alternative is possible. amitrasya is a genitive (of/for the enemy) taken with vṛtti-kara. The grouping of the two ca is uncertain.

words.gloss: of the one with a river fort and the one with a mountain fort
from the one with a river fort

hindi: नदी-दुर्ग वाले और पर्वत-दुर्ग वाले में से नदी-दुर्ग वाले से भूमि-लाभ श्रेष्ठ है।
english: Of [the one] with a river fort and [the one] with a mountain fort, the acquisition of land from [the one] with a river fort is better.

text_flags.why: doubled b: stray letter (the previous word nadī.durgīyād already ends in d)

notes: Same pattern as unit 28; the stray b (ब्भूमि) is not repeated in the Devanagari reading either.

words.gloss: by elephants, posts, crossings, embankment-dams and boats

hindi: क्योंकि नदी-दुर्ग हाथियों, खम्भों, संक्रमों, सेतु-बन्धों, नावों से साध्य है, और जल अस्थायी गहराई वाला, बह जाने वाला है।
english: For a river fort is to be accomplished by elephants, posts, crossings, embankment-dams and boats, and the water, of non-permanent depth, is flowing off.
notes: The items of the dvandva are taken as five (hasti, stambha, saṅkrama, setu-bandha, nau); hasti-stambha as one item ("elephant-posts") is also possible. sādhya = to be accomplished/overcome (the object not stated). anitya-gāmbhīrya and avasrāvi are taken as adjectives of udakam; "avasrāvi" is literally "flowing off/down".

hindi: किन्तु पार्वत सुरक्षा योग्य, कठिनाई से अवरोध करने योग्य, कठिन चढ़ाई वाला है, और एक के टूटने पर सबका वध नहीं, और शिला-वृक्षों का छोड़ना बड़ा अपकार करने वालों का।
english: But the [fort] of the mountain is easy to guard, hard to blockade, with a difficult ascent; and when one is broken, [there is] not the destruction of all; and the release of rocks and trees [is that] of those who do great harm.
notes: "Fort" (durga) is understood. The printed sv.ārakṣam is su-ārakṣam (sv. = su before ā, the dot marking the compound boundary), not a typo. bhagne ca ekasmin: "one" (part/fort/post) is not named. The last clause is elliptical: the genitive mahā-apakāriṇām may mean the rocks and trees are a means of (or are hurled upon) those doing great harm; the text does not say, so it is rendered literally.

words.gloss: from fighters in low ground and on dry ground

hindi: निम्न भूमि और स्थल में लड़ने वालों में से निम्न भूमि में लड़ने वालों से भूमि-लाभ श्रेष्ठ है।
english: Of those who fight in low ground and those who fight on dry ground, the acquisition of land from those who fight in low ground is better.
notes: nimna = low ground; sthala = dry ground. The ablative plural is read as partitive, as in unit 26.

words.gloss: those who fight in low ground
those who fight on dry ground
fighting in every place and time

hindi: क्योंकि निम्न भूमि में लड़ने वालों के देश और काल अवरुद्ध हैं, किन्तु स्थल में लड़ने वाले सब देश और काल में लड़ने वाले हैं।
english: For those who fight in low ground have place and time restricted, but those who fight on dry ground fight in every place and time.
notes: uparuddha = obstructed, restricted. deśa = place.

words.gloss: from diggers and fighters in the sky

hindi: खोदने वालों और आकाश में लड़ने वालों में से खोदने वालों से भूमि-लाभ श्रेष्ठ है।
english: Of diggers and those who fight in the sky, the acquisition of land from the diggers is better.
notes: khanaka = digger (miner); ākāśa-yodhin literally "sky-fighter" (fighting in the open air); unit 37 says they fight with a weapon only. The ablative plural is read as partitive.

words.gloss: those who fight in the sky

hindi: क्योंकि खोदने वाले खात से और शस्त्र से दोनों प्रकार से लड़ते हैं, आकाश में लड़ने वाले शस्त्र से ही।
english: For diggers fight in both ways, with excavation and with a weapon; those who fight in the sky, with a weapon only.
notes: khāta = excavation (trench, pit); the verb of the last clause is not stated.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. mid. √labh

words.gloss: knower of the science of wealth

hindi: इस प्रकार वालों से पृथ्वी प्राप्त करता हुआ अर्थशास्त्र को जानने वाला, मिले हुए और दूसरों की अपेक्षा विशेषता प्राप्त करता है।
english: The knower of the science of wealth, obtaining the earth from those of this kind, attains superiority over the allied and over the others.

text_flags.why: possible stray y: evaṃvidha, "of this kind", not a form of vidhya

notes: "The science of wealth" is the title word artha-śāstra, taken literally. The ablatives saṃhitebhyaḥ parebhyaḥ are read as ablatives of comparison ("than/over"); "the others" = pare, not necessarily "enemies" (glossary 9.2). Verse (two half-lines).
